value.rationale: The known first six-root prime supplies a canonical, nonarbitrary place to test persistence of several roots in a valuation problem. The presence of six roots modulo p does not determine whether any are singular, which would permit different prime-power counts. Certifying each nondegenerate branch gives the exact class count at every depth and concrete second-level representatives usable in subsequent valuation calculations. The valuable part is this classification, not the reproduced census or the application of a textbook theorem without checking its premises.
residual_risks: The repair makes no claims about larger multiplicities, other primes, non-unit indices or new lifting methods.
